items.title: Anwar: MA63 is a national promise, must not be seen as only affecting Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 17 — The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) is a national pledge or pact that must be respected and implemented, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said that MA63 is a solemn promise made by the previous leaders of Malaysia. Also present were Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.

items.title: Malaysia Armed Forces to add Cyber Force as fourth service by 2030
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is set to make history by establishing a Cyber Force as its fourth service by 2030, in a strategic move to confront evolving threats in the modern security landscape. Armed Forces Chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move was prompted by the fact that cyberspace and the electromagnetic domain have increasingly become arenas of competition and warfare on the global stage. To this end, he said a dedicated team known as the Cyber Force Nucleus Team has been formed to spearhead planning, coordination, organisational transformation preparations, and capability development towards the force's official establishment.

items.title: BUDI Diesel subsidy eligibility now transferable to non-family users, says Anwar
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 17 — The government has agreed to expand the BUDI Madani Diesel (BUDI Diesel) eligibility transfer facility, allowing registered owners of private diesel vehicles to transfer their eligibility to any eligible actual user, effective immediately. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said previously, the transfer of eligibility was restricted to immediate family members. In addition, Anwar said registered owners of more than one private diesel vehicle were allowed to transfer the monthly BUDI Diesel eligibility of those vehicles to a maximum of three other vehicles.

items.title: US House passes Russia sanctions bill championed by late Senator Graham
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US House of Representatives on Wednesday passed a sweeping sanctions and tariff bill intended to increase economic pressure on Russia over its invasion of Ukraine, sending the bill to President Donald Trump to sign into law nearly 1-1/2 years after the late Senator Lindsey Graham introduced it. The bill, now called the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026" to honour the South Carolina Republican, passed the Senate last month. The legislation targets Russia's energy and defence industries, as well as its "shadow fleet" of tankers that evade existing sanctions.

items.title: DKU accuses Negeri Sembilan exco of treason, coup attempt against Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU) has accused the Negri Sembilan state executive council of treason and attempting to overthrow Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. The letter was addressed to Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and copied to members of the state executive council, the state secretary and the state legal adviser. It referred to the ' Kenyataan Media Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan — Keputusan Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri, Negeri Sembilan Bil 6 Tahun 2026' dated Sept 15.

items.title: Ringgit opens slightly lower vs US dollar after hawkish FOMC outcome
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Thursday as the greenback strengthened following a hawkish outcome from the United States (US) Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting overnight. The US Federal Reserve (Fed) raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75 per cent to 4.00 per cent, which it had previously forecast at 3.50 per cent to 3.75 per cent, marking its first rate hike since 2023. He noted that the move has helped to drive the US dollar higher, with the US dollar index (DXY) hovering at 100.322 points, while the two- and ten-year US Treasury yields rose seven and two basis points to 4.74 per cent and 5.02 per cent, respectively.

items.title: Samoa charges two over killing of Australian in Vietnam
items.summary: SYDNEY: Police in Samoa have charged two men over the killing of a Sydney gangland figure outside a seafood restaurant in Vietnam in May, they said Thursday. The men – one a New Zealander and the other a Samoan – face a maximum penalty of life imprisonment after being charged with conspiracy to murder, Australia's Federal Police and Samoan law enforcement said. Samoan police allege they conspired to murder Lorenzo Lemalu, purportedly leader of Sydney's so-called "Coconut Cartel" organised crime group.

items.title: 26 areas record unhealthy air quality nationwide this morning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 26 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today. According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System portal, Tasek Ipoh recorded an API of 182 while Seri Manjung followed closely at 179. Several other areas including Minden, Penang (157), Seberang Jaya (155), Taiping (157), Cheras, (157), Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (156), Putrajaya (157) and Nilai (157) also registered unhealthy.

items.title: Former Negri Sembilan MB backs Tuanku Muhriz as lawmakers question exco statement on royal succession
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Former Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has called on the people of the state to stand behind Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, as two Pakatan Harapan lawmakers questioned whether a state executive council statement affirming his removal represents the official position of the state government. “Reject leaders who betray the royal institution and violate the (state) constitution. Bahau assemblyman Teo Kok Seong, a former state exco member, meanwhile questioned whether a joint statement by exco members could be regarded as the official position of the state government.

items.title: Anwar, Abang Johari witness Bintulu Port handover to Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg yesterday witnessed the official handover of Bintulu Port to the Sarawak state government from the federal government, marking a new chapter in the management of the strategic port. “With the coming into force of Act 858 and Act 859 on September 1, Bintulu Port officially changed its status from a federal port to a state port under the jurisdiction of the Sarawak government,” the statement said. The transition also saw the dissolution of the Bintulu Port Authority (LPB), with the port authority functions taken over by the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak), a state statutory body established under the Port Authorities Ordinance 1961.

items.title: Anwar: RM500 domestic flight aid for new students travelling between peninsula and Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The government has announced a one-off RM500 special assistance for domestic flight ticket purchases for every eligible new student of public higher education institutions (IPTA) for the September or October intake this year. Anwar had earlier announced that Sarawak's interim special grant would be increased to RM1.5 billion this year, up from RM600 million previously. He said the Federal Government would continue engaging with the Sabah and Sarawak state governments to finalise a sustainable formula to determine the annual Special Grant rate.

items.title: Goldsmith shop robbed of RM1mil for second time in two years [WATCH]
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: Four masked men armed with hammers and sharp weapons robbed a goldsmith shop inside a shopping centre here last night. Kuala Muda police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said police received a call from the public shortly after the incident. He said two men entered the goldsmith shop and were believed to have taken gold items before fleeing, while their two accomplices waited about 20m from the premises.

items.title: Wall Street swings after Fed hikes interest rate to battle inflation
items.summary: NEW YORK: Wall Street whipsawed on Wednesday after the US Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate for the first time in over three years to fight stubbornly high inflation stemming from soaring crude oil prices during the US-Israeli war on Iran. "As widely expected, the Fed hiked interest rates for the first time in more than three years," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 101.92 points, or 0.20 per cent, to 51,991.19, the S&P 500 gained 21.09 points, or 0.28 per cent, to 7,606.82 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 170.49 points, or 0.66 per cent, to 26,152.06.

items.title: US again denies Palestinian leader Abbas visa to attend UN assembly
items.summary: WASHINGTON, (United States): The United States has denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, a source familiar with the case said Wednesday. It is the second straight year the US has denied a visa to Abbas. — AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: NASA scan discovers new, 'once in a century' Moon crater
items.summary: WASHINGTON, (United States): A researcher at NASA has found a massive, recently-formed crater on the Moon, a rare occurrence that only happens "once in a century or even longer," according to scientists. The crater, dubbed "McGetchin," measures 730 feet (222 meters) wide, NASA said in a blog post. "Scientists estimate that an impact of this magnitude happens on the Moon about once in a century or even longer," NASA said in the blog post.

items.title: Protecting our whistleblowers
items.summary: THE decision in Norhaida binti Ramli v Majlis Agama Islam Wilayah Persekutuan & 2 Ors (High Court, Kuala Lumpur) is significant because it gives practical meaning to a principle that is often stated but insufficiently enforced: a whistleblower who exposes suspected wrongdoing should not become the victim of the system to which the disclosure is made. The case has been described as a landmark Malaysian decision under the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010 (Act 711). The potential whistleblower asks: What will happen to me if I report this?

items.title: Mondelez strengthens Malaysia supply chain amid cocoa price surge
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Mondelez International is taking greater control of its chocolate supply chain in Malaysia by producing cocoa crumb locally, amid triple-digit growth in cocoa prices in recent years. Mondelez International Malaysia and Singapore managing director Simon Crowther said the new facility allows the company to produce both chocolate liquid and cocoa crumb at the same site before combining them to make finished chocolate products. Cocoa crumb is a mixture of cocoa, milk and cocoa butter, which is combined with chocolate liquid before being moulded into the Cadbury Dairy Milk bar familiar to consumers.

items.title: 'No doubt' of climate change role in deadly China-Nepal flood
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Climate change was a core factor in last month's deadly glacial mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border that killed more than 1,400 people and left at least 6,600 missing, scientists said Thursday. However, scientists from the World Weather Attribution (WWA) group said the disaster was not caused by a single extreme weather event, rather a "compound crisis" shaped by long-term warming, glacier retreat, permafrost thaw and geological instability. Report co-author Walter Immerzeel, a mountain hydrologist at Utrecht University, said the region was undergoing "fundamental, irreversible shifts", with glacier retreat and permafrost degradation undermining mountain stability.

items.title: Korean Air records double-digit Penang cargo growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Korean Air Lines Co Ltd recorded double-digit growth in export cargo volume from Penang in the first half of 2026 driven by demand for high-value semiconductor and electronics shipments bound for South Korea and the Americas. Korean Air regional manager for Malaysia, Brunei and Bangladesh Kang Sang Bum said cargo demand from Penang continue to increase. Korean Air's cargo division, Korean Air Cargo operates six weekly freighter frequencies from Penang using Boeing B747-400F and B777F aircraft across four dedicated route loops.

items.title: Malaysia, India move to rebalance trade, review FTA
items.summary: Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the issue of Malaysia's trade surplus with India was a key topic during his meeting with India's trade minister here. In 2025, Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of RM25.37 billion with India, with total bilateral trade reaching RM79.33 billion, a 5.0 per cent decline from RM83.5 billion (US$18.25 billion) in 2024. He said Malaysia was also looking at ways to strengthen trade between Asean and India, alongside efforts to enhance the bilateral trade framework between Malaysia and India.

items.title: Johari: Malaysia steps up palm oil push in India to counter 'propaganda'
items.summary: Johari said Malaysia, the world's second-largest palm oil exporter after Indonesia, will continue strengthening its presence in the Indian market by leveraging its integrated upstream and downstream industries. He said Malaysia remained the world's second-largest palm oil exporter after Indonesia, with its production supported by an established upstream plantation sector and a sizeable downstream industry producing higher-value palm-based products. "Malaysia is still the second-largest exporter of palm oil.

items.title: Betancourt family retains majority share in firm at heart of US-Venezuela oil deal
items.summary: CARACAS: The family of Alejandro Betancourt, a contentious businessman at the centre of a massive US-Venezuela oil deal, retains the majority stake in his company NABEP, which is overseeing the agreement, the firm told AFP Wednesday. "The Betancourt family remains the majority shareholder of NABEP," a company spokesperson told AFP via email. NABEP is Venezuela's second-largest private oil company and will operate 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields with proven reserves of approximately 65 billion barrels under the agreement announced last month.

items.title: Kim's sister says only 'idiots' believe N. Korea will give up nukes
items.summary: SEOUL: The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said Thursday that the country's nuclear-armed status was "absolute", calling those hoping for its denuclearisation "idiots". North Korea has legally enshrined its status as a nuclear weapons state, with its leadership declaring the country's nuclear arsenal permanent and irreversible. US President Donald Trump recently said Pyongyang possesses 57 "very powerful" nuclear weapons, with Seoul putting the figure at between 80 and 120.

items.title: Trump threatens EU over 'hostile' Canada association plan
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump threatened on Wednesday to cut trade with the European Union after the bloc proposed to make Canada its first ever associate member. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen raised the prospect a day before Canadian leader Mark Carney was due to address the European Parliament. Von der Leyen pitched closer cooperation on tech, defence and energy to Carney, who became the first non-European head of government to attend the annual "State of the European Union" speech.

items.title: Netanyahu steps up threats against directors of Gaza documentary 'NAZA'
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed on Wednesday to pass a law to revoke the citizenship of anyone who defames Israel's soldiers, his latest threat against the Israeli directors of "NAZA", a documentary about soldiers' killing of Gaza civilians. Directed by Israeli journalists Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, NAZA alleges that mass civilian deaths were routinely built into Israeli targeting decisions in Gaza, something Netanyahu and the military reject. The film, which won a major prize at the Venice Film Festival on Saturday, takes its title from an Israeli military term for expected "collateral casualties" and is built around anonymous interviews with intelligence officers and soldiers.

items.title: US Fed raises rates to tackle 'too high' inflation, irking Trump
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, defying President Donald Trump's demand for cuts, as central bank chief Kevin Warsh stressed the need to combat inflation that has been "too high" for "too long." The Fed's Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously to raise rates by 25 basis points to between 3.75 and 4.00 per cent. And Wednesday's rate hike may not be the last – the vast majority of Fed policymakers indicated that at least one more rate hike was likely necessary before the end of the year, according to their Summary of Economic Projections (SEP).

items.title: India, Pakistan trade blame and protests over navy collision
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Arch-rivals India and Pakistan traded blame on Wednesday for a collision at sea between two vessels operated by their navies, summoning each other's top diplomats to lodge "strong" protests. Pakistan's foreign ministry said the incident took place on Tuesday while its navy was conducting a biennial exercise in its exclusive economic zone (EEZ). A senior Indian official said that the incident happened late Tuesday in the north of the Arabian Sea.

items.title: US drone maker Powerus signs Pakistan Army MOU, gets initial order
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: US drone firm Powerus has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Pakistan Army that includes an initial drone-related order, co-founder Brett Velicovich told Reuters on Wednesday. As part of that MOU, we received an initial order for power systems," Velicovich said, speaking in Islamabad. Trump's sons Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump own a stake in Aureus through an investment fund called American Ventures, according to US regulatory filings.

items.title: Epstein survivors sue his estate over child pornography collection
items.summary: MEXICO CITY: Two women whose images as girls were found in pornography seized from Jeffrey Epstein filed a class action lawsuit on Wednesday seeking damages from the late sex offender's estate for individuals featured in his collection of thousands of pictures and videos of child sexual abuse material. Others were shown in over ten thousand downloaded videos and images of child sexual abuse material and other pornography taken from the late financier's properties, according to the action. The lawsuit was filed against Epstein's former attorney Darren Indyke and his former accountant Richard Kahn, the co-executors of the Epstein estate.

items.title: Malaysia’s OPR stays at 2.75pc: What does it mean for your loans, savings and spendings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) has kept its Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent, maintaining the rate for a seventh consecutive meeting. What does the OPR do The OPR is Bank Negara’s key monetary policy rate. How does Bank Negara decide the OPR?

items.title: New MyKad to be issued from today
items.summary: THE National Registration Department (NRD) will begin issuing the new generation of MyKad boasting 53 security features, up from 23 previously, starting today. The NRD said the new MyKad was an evolution of the national identity document aimed at keeping pace with changing times. It added that 40 NRD branches had been equipped with printing facilities to issue the new MyKad.

items.title: Keretapi Sarong unites Malaysians in colours
items.summary: The event also featured cultural performances, traditional games and community activities. "I see people wearing traditional clothes, and they look beautiful. I like traditional clothing, and I enjoy sharing traditional attire with everyone."

items.title: Houthis report Saudi strikes as Riyadh accuses them of targeting Makkah
items.summary: RIYADH: Yemen's Houthis reported fresh Saudi airstrikes on Wednesday, as Riyadh accused the group of launching a "cowardly" attack targeting Islam's holy city of Makkah. Renewed fighting between the Houthis and Yemen's Riyadh-backed government has dragged in the kingdom, after the Houthis declared a maritime blockade on Saudi ships in the Red Sea. Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemned the targeting of Makkah as a "cowardly terrorist attack" and reaffirmed the kingdom's right to "defend the security of the two holy mosques, the pilgrims, and the entire Saudi territory."

items.title: US House holds Epstein associate Leon Black in contempt
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US House of Representatives held billionaire investor Leon Black in contempt of Congress on Wednesday for defying subpoenas issued in its investigation into notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Leon Black defied two subpoenas, and the US House of Representatives acted swiftly to find him in contempt of Congress," panel chairman Jamie Comer said in a statement. His lawyers called the House action "outrageous", accused lawmakers of rushing the process and said they would continue a court challenge to the subpoenas, US media reported.

items.title: KLIA cuts e-hailing entry fees to RM2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The entry fees for e-hailing vehicles at Kuala Lumpur International Airport have been standardised at RM2, inclusive of tax, across Terminals 1 and 2 effective yesterday. MAHB said the enhanced e-hailing facilities introduced at Terminal 1 last month as part of its improvement initiatives have recorded encouraging operational improvements. KLIA senior general manager for passenger experience Abd Hasman Abd Muhimin said the continued enhancements to the e-hailing facilities reflect the airport operator's commitment to improving the overall passenger journey while ensuring that airport operations remain orderly, efficient and responsive to evolving needs.

items.title: Satellite data shows major ice losses for Greenland and Antarctica
items.summary: NEW RESEARCH based on satellite data going back to the 1970s has documented major polar ice losses in Greenland and Antarctica — home to Earth's two great ice sheets — that have contributed to rising global sea levels. Between 1979 and 2023, according to data from 27 satellite missions, Greenland and Antarctica lost a combined 11.3 trillion tons of ice, adding 1.24 inches (3.14 cm) to the worldwide sea-level rise. The study, employing the longest satellite data record of changes in ice sheets ever gathered to give the most complete account to date of ice loss in Greenland and Antarctica, was conducted by the Ice Sheet Mass Balance Inter-comparison Exercise team, an international group of polar scientists.

items.title: Nepal raises flood missing toll by nearly 1,000 people to 6,150
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Nepal's disaster authority said Wednesday it had sharply revised up the number of people considered missing after the August 26 flood to 6,150, following data collection and verification in affected districts. "We have been collecting details on the missing people from the district offices, and revised the data after verification," disaster authority spokeswoman Shanti Mahat told AFP. Across the border in China, the toll is 43 dead and 519 missing, according to state media.

items.title: Gaza apartment block collapse leaves 21 dead
items.summary: GAZA CITY, Palestinian Territories: Gaza authorities said Wednesday that 21 people including five children had died after an apartment building collapsed from damage sustained in earlier Israeli strikes. At Gaza City's Al-Shifa Hospital, AFP journalists saw weeping men carrying children's bodies wrapped in white shrouds. The building, which was housing more than 100 displaced people, had sustained damage from previous Israeli strikes, the civil defence agency said.

items.title: Police confirm body found in Perak waters is missing angler
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 16 —Police have confirmed that the body of a man found floating in the waters off Hutan Melintang, Perak, this morning is one of the three anglers missing since Monday. Klang Utara police chief ACP Ramsay Embol said the body was identified as Mohd Sharil Abd Rahman, 43, following identification by next-of-kin. Ramsay said the joint SAR operation to locate the two remaining missing victims is ongoing.

items.title: Diesel, RON97 and unsubsidised RON95 prices up by RM0.35 for Sept 17-23 period
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 35 sen per litre for the Sept 17-23 period, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said. In a statement today, MOF said the retail price of RON97 would increase to RM4.85 per litre from RM4.50, while unsubsidised RON95 would rise to RM4.37 from RM4.02 and unsubsidised diesel to RM5.27 from RM4.92. The ministry said the increase in global fuel prices was driven by heightened tensions in West Asia amid the conflict, which has entered its 200th day.

items.title: PM Anwar: Malaysia supports and appreciates Saudi Arabia’s efforts following drone interception in Mecca
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia has expressed its support for Saudi Arabia following the successful interception of a drone near Mecca, asserting that any attempt to threaten the security and sanctity of Islam’s holiest city is completely unacceptable. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia appreciates the swift action taken to safeguard the safety of residents and pilgrims in Mecca. “I have been following reports on a drone that was successfully intercepted near Makkah al-Mukarramah.

items.title: Selangor MB: Follow-up haze measures to be reviewed on Friday
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — The Selangor government will review follow-up measures to address the deteriorating haze situation, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said the matter would be discussed in detail, based on reports from all relevant parties, at the Selangor State Executive Council meeting scheduled for Friday. Six areas in Selangor recorded Air Pollution Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4.30 pm today.

items.title: Haze alert: 38 areas in Peninsular Malaysia record unhealthy readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A total of 38 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recorded unhealthy Air Pollution Index (API) readings as of 5 pm today. According to the API management system (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor - Johan Setia (183), Shah Alam (170), Petaling Jaya (164), Klang (160) as well as Banting and Kuala Selangor (159), two areas in Kuala Lumpur - Cheras (174) and Batu Muda (170), three areas in Negeri Sembilan - Nilai (170), Seremban (165) and Port Dickson (148), along with Putrajaya (170) - recorded API readings at the unhealthy level. Down south in Johor, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings - Tangkak (134), Kluang (124) and Batu Pahat (103), as well as three areas in Melaka - Bukit Rambai (155), Alor Gajah (153) and Bandaraya Melaka (145).

items.title: New-generation MyKad applications open tomorrow with enhanced security features
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The National Registration Department (NRD) has unveiled the new-generation MyKad with a redesigned appearance and enhanced security features. The new card incorporates several security elements on both its front and back, including a Dynamic Security Hologram and transparent window on the front. He said the new MyKad has about 50 additional security features, which will be introduced in phases.

items.title: Malaysia Day: PM Anwar calls for renewed commitment to unity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia Day serves as a reminder that the nation was built on a covenant between the government and the people, between the regions and the Federation, and between loyalty and justice, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Happy Malaysia Day!" he said.

items.title: Woman killed, sister and motorcyclist seriously injured after lorry hits their stalled car in Nilai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A woman was killed while her sister and a motorcyclist were seriously injured after a lorry crashed into their broken-down car at Kilometre 284.4 of the North-South Expressway northbound near Nilai this morning. Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the district traffic complaints counter received information about the accident from the Nilai district police operations room at 9.01am. Johari said a 22-year-old man riding a Honda RS 150 arrived at the scene and tried to help the woman move the vehicle.

items.title: Police: Body found in Perak waters, believed to be missing Perak angler
items.summary: Mohd Rahimi said those who survived included Mohd Shairazi Abdul Aziz, 43, Mohd Rizal Mohamad Sadali and Muhd Hamiszar Punirain, both 45, as well as boat skipper Zulfikalnain Awang, 47. “The three anglers still missing are Muhamad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman, 43, and Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamad, 49,” he said. Earlier, Mohd Rahimi accompanied Selangor deputy police chief DCP Mohd Zaini Abu Hassan to inspect the on-scene command post (PKTK) before visiting the victims’ families around Sementa Jetty here.

items.title: Malaysia to seek preventive measures, diplomatic cooperation over transboundary haze, says Zahid
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 16 — Malaysia prioritises long-term diplomatic cooperation and early preventive measures over seeking compensation from neighbouring countries in addressing the issue of transboundary haze, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee Chairman, said a prudent and structured diplomatic approach is the most effective way to address sensitive issues among Asean member states while ensuring optimal technical coordination. Also present were Sarawak Deputy Premier and Chairman of the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN), Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, and Deputy Minister of Rural and Regional Development, Datuk Rubiah Wang.

items.title: Anwar to review impact of electricity bill increase at special meeting tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A special meeting will be held tomorrow with the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), the Energy Commission (EC), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and the Ministry of Finance (MoF). The meeting will review immediate mitigation measures to reduce the impact of the electricity bill increase on affected households. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that upon his return from India and the Maldives, his attention remained focused on the people’s concerns regarding the recent increase in electricity bills.

items.title: Policeman injured while chasing 4WD involved in Kluang cable theft case
items.summary: Kluang deputy police chief Superintendent Nik Mohd Azmi Husin said the incident is believed to have occurred at 5.54am when two policemen on motorcycles were chasing a Mitsubishi vehicle. He said the suspect, believed to be involved in an earlier cable theft incident, had an uncut cable at the rear of the vehicle. Nik Mohd Azmi was responding to a video posted on Threads showing two policemen chasing a red Mitsubishi pick-up truck in Kluang town.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan DOE ramps up enforcement as haze hits unhealthy levels
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 16 — The Negeri Sembilan Department of Environment (DOE) is stepping up ground-level monitoring, particularly on open burning activities, following worsening haze conditions in several districts in the state. State DOE director Abdul Aziz Parmin said other sources being closely monitored included factories, quarries, motor vehicles, development projects, land clearing and any activities that could contribute to dust emissions and cause air pollution. He said all actions related to the haze situation would be referred to the National Haze Action Plan, while at the state level, the department would continuously update the State Disaster Management Committee on the situation.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: My views on Najib’s pardon given honestly
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 —Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she had expressed her views on former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon application during the Pardons Board meeting on Sept 11, after reviewing the written opinion of the Attorney General. The statement was issued in response to remarks by Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said regarding the deferment of Najib’s pardon application. Hannah said she had expressed her views in her capacity as the minister responsible for the Federal Territories.

items.title: Schools advised to stagger students seeking medical checks, says Perak health exco
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 16 — The Perak government has advised schools to coordinate with District Health Offices and relevant health facilities before bringing large numbers of students for medical examinations following an outbreak. The advice came after a boarding school in Ipoh brought 57 students with Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) to a nearby health clinic simultaneously, despite being advised to bring them in stages. Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said bringing symptomatic students in stages would help prevent congestion at health facilities and reduce the risk of infection transmission.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng: Umno no longer brings value to Penang government amid cooperation with Perikatan, PAS
items.summary: Lim said Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow appeared more focused on criticising him than addressing Umno’s recent attacks on PH, creating what he described as an impression that Chow feared Umno might quit the state government. “Instead of hitting back at Umno for working with the opposition PN, Chow chose to criticise me,” Lim said, adding that Penang PH leaders should not be afraid of offending “an extremist Umno” that he claimed had indulged in divisive rhetoric against non-Muslim minorities and shown little inclusivity toward non-Malays. Even without Umno’s two assemblymen, Lim said, PH would still command a two‑thirds majority in the Penang legislative assembly.

items.title: Perak exco: 46 students at Influenza A cluster school suffer flu-like illness
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 16 — Forty-six students at a boarding school in Ipoh have been diagnosed with influenza-like illness (ILI) following an Influenza A cluster detected at the school, Perak Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman A. Sivanesan said. He said the cases were identified after health officials screened and assessed 61 students with symptoms up to Sept 14, while 14 others were found to have upper respiratory tract infections and one had conjunctivitis. According to him, the school had first brought 57 symptomatic students to a nearby health clinic on Monday, before the figure rose to 61 when an additional 39 symptomatic students were brought in yesterday.

items.title: Raja Muda of Selangor, MACC chief commissioner discuss anti-corruption initiatives
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — Efforts to strengthen the fight against corruption were among the matters discussed by Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman. The MACC said the matter was discussed when Tengku Amir Shah granted an audience to Abd Halim at Istana Selangor, Bukit Kiara, last Monday. In a statement today, the commission said Tengku Amir Shah was also briefed on its latest developments and ongoing initiatives, particularly those relating to anti-corruption efforts in Selangor.

items.title: Sanusi: Too early for seat talks as Kedah PAS, Umno explore political cooperation
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 16 — Kedah PAS and Umno are focusing on creating a positive environment for further discussions on political cooperation, with no requests yet made over seat allocations, Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor reportedly said. The Umno delegation was led by Kedah Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Mahdzir Khalid and Alor Setar Umno division chief and former Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Bashah Md Hanipah. PAS was represented by Kedah commissioner and PAS Central Ulama Council chief Datuk Ahmad Yahya, deputy commissioner II Dr Ahmad Fakhruddin Sheikh Fakhrurazi and Kedah secretary Senator Musoddaq Ahmad.

items.title: Penang air quality hits unhealthy levels statewide, Minden records API of 167
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 16 — Air quality at all four monitoring stations in Penang reached unhealthy levels as of 11am today, with Minden recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 167. State Housing and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said Balik Pulau recorded an API reading of 164, followed by Seberang Jaya at 162 and Seberang Perai at 160. He said Minden and Balik Pulau had registered unhealthy readings over the past 24 hours, while readings in Seberang Jaya and Seberang Perai had risen from moderate to unhealthy levels.

items.title: Police: Sri Petaling bomb scare turns out to be team-building game equipment left behind by worker
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A suspicious plastic box found unattended in front of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Sri Petaling earlier today contained toy building blocks belonging to a company that organises training and team-building programmes, police said today. Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said police were contacted by a company director, who informed them that the unattended plastic box belonged to his company. “Investigations found that the box had been left behind by a company employee and contained 20 plastic toy blocks from a game called ‘Radioactive Bomb’, which are used as equipment for group team-building activities.

items.title: MA63 still binding, no ‘new deal’ needed, says Armizan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 16 — The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) did not cease to exist upon the enactment of the Federal Constitution but remains in force, with the commitments and responsibilities contained therein continuing to be relevant and binding on all parties, said Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. “This term reaffirms the commitment and responsibility of all parties that agreed to sign the agreement to form the Federation of Malaysia,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with Malaysia Day today. Armizan said Malaysia, which was formed in 1963, has now reached 63 years, although Sept 16 only became an important date in the official national calendar and was officially celebrated as Malaysia Day from 2010.
